extracted.intended_audience: ML researchers and benchmark designers evaluating LLM mathematical reasoning
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating a static benchmark of IMO-level mathematical problems for LLMs, with a deterministic numeric-answer track and a decomposed proof track for stepwise automated grading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve Olympiad difficulty while eliminating evaluation noise
rubrics_metrics.description: RIMO is designed to "preserve peak Olympiad difficulty while eliminating this evaluation noise."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The benchmark must keep genuine IMO-level hardness but remove sources of grading ambiguity and bias (e.g., heterogeneous answer formats or learned judges). RIMO unifies a noise-free integer track with a rigorously graded proof track to provide a high-resolution, reproducible yardstick.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIMO-N: single unique integer answers (deterministic exact-match grading)
rubrics_metrics.description: "RIMO-N consists of 335 problems, carefully remade to yield a single, unique integer answer. This allows for deterministic, O(1) string-match grading, removing any reliance on model-based judges."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design items so the canonical solution is a single integer; grading collapses to constant-time string comparison, eliminating need for symbolic normalization or learned judges. Track composition given (335 problems across algebra/geometry/number theory/combinatorics).

rubrics_metrics.name: RIMO-P: decomposed proof problems with expert-checked solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: "RIMO-P contains 456 proof problems with expert-checked solutions, which are decomposed into a sequence of sub-problems to evaluate the step-by-step reasoning process via an automated grading system."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use official or expert-verified solutions to decompose proofs into 1–4 sub-problems (longer solutions → 3–4 steps). The decomposition scaffolds evaluation of intermediate lemmas while preserving the original final goal in the last sub-problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remaking principles for RIMO-N items (faithful but unambiguous rewrites)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Remaking is never a cosmetic tweak to the last line: intermediate hypotheses are tightened when ambiguity appears, variables are renamed for coherence, and objectives are reframed, yet the logical core and difficulty of the source problem remain intact."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rewriting, preserve logical core and difficulty; tighten ambiguous hypotheses, rename variables for clarity, and reframe objectives so the item admits a unique integer. Examples: converting concurrency proofs into 'how many common points' or classification problems into 'compute value of a+b+c over every such triple.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Source verification and acceptance criteria for ground truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems are assembled from IMO contest papers and shortlist booklets, with solutions reconciled across multiple sources (official shortlist solutions, AoPS-Wiki, YouTube expositions, ParSe transcripts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortlist problems retain the jury's official integer. For contest problems without an official key, accept only when at least two of three independent community sources return exactly the same answer; any disagreement triggers manual adjudication and usually exclusion. Multi-source cross-checking ensures reliability of ground truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIMO-P decomposition rule (1–4 sub-problems; final preserves original goal)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The complexity of a reference proof determines its decomposition into one to four sub-problems, with longer solutions typically yielding a three or four-step logical pathway. ... the final sub-problem in every sequence preserves the original problem’s main goal."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decompose official proofs into consecutive sub-steps that represent intermediate lemmas; ensure the final step corresponds to the original problem objective. This scaffolded design enables granular assessment of stepwise reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIMO-P sequential grading protocol (consecutive sub-problems solved)
rubrics_metrics.description: "We grade a proof by the number of consecutive sub-problems solved correctly." (Formalized as P = (1/N) Σ_i Si/Xi where Si is number of consecutively correct sub-solutions for problem i and Xi is total sub-problems.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score each problem by the fraction of consecutively-correct sub-steps achieved; average over problems to get final performance P. This emphasizes contiguous correctness (an error breaks the chain for that problem).

rubrics_metrics.name: RIMO-P Judger rules: strict, local step evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt instructs: "Only approve if the solution is mathematically correct, logically sound, and free of gaps or unjustified steps." and "Judge ONLY the candidate sub-solution at this step. Check correctness, logical validity, and consistency with the problem and official solution."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be strict: any error, gap, or unjustified claim ⇒ mark incorrect. Do not grade future steps. Evaluator must respond in strict JSON with keys 'verdict' and 'reason' using only {"verdict":"correct"} or {"verdict":"incorrect"}; 'reason' must be a short sentence. Evaluate each sub-step only against problem + official complete solution + candidate sub-solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deterministic evaluation protocol for model generations (reproducibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: All generations use a single greedy decode with zero temperature (T = 0) under the same prompt template and context window; this reproduces the protocol used by earlier benchmarks and removes prompt engineering confounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use greedy decoding (T=0) and fixed prompt/context to ensure reproducibility across runs; report Pass@1 accuracy (or analogous deterministic metrics) rather than sampling-based metrics that introduce variance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact-match grading and avoidance of learned judges for numeric track
rubrics_metrics.description: RIMO-N’s single-integer format allows for deterministic string-match grading, ensuring efficiency, reproducibility, and elimination of grading bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer exact-match rule-based graders for numeric outputs to avoid expression normalization, learned-judge noise, and stylistic penalties. When possible, rewrite problems to a uniform answer format to permit exact-match checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and handling of binary (0/1) subset
rubrics_metrics.description: RIMO-N contains 96 problems whose ground-truth integer happens to be 0 or 1; roughly two-thirds are T/F formulations while the remainder ask for numeric extrema evaluating to 0 or 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track and optionally evaluate this binary subset separately: binary outputs reduce search space and inflate accuracy; report both full-set and binary-subset performance to diagnose how much difficulty comes from locating integers versus binary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multi-source adjudication and manual review on disagreements
rubrics_metrics.description: "Any disagreement triggers manual adjudication and usually leads to exclusion."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When community sources disagree about a contest problem's answer, escalate to manual adjudication; if unresolved, exclude the item to maintain dataset reliability. Prefer retaining shortlist items with official keys where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omni-Math style LLM judge rubric (equivalence-focused, but binary strictness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Omni-Math judge prompt: judge whether the student's answer "captures the same meaning as the reference answer"; tasks include (A) identify mathematical or notational equivalence (pay attention to LaTeX), (B) provide a justification; "Equivalence Judgement is only TRUE or FALSE. The answer is FALSE even if the student's final answer is almost correct with a minor mistake."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using an LLM-based equivalence judge: focus on mathematical/notational equivalence, extract boxed final answer, output a professional teaching-style report with explicit TRUE/FALSE equivalence and a justification. Be aware that this approach penalizes near-misses (treats almost-correct as incorrect) and can introduce stylistic/equivalence errors (as illustrated by GPT-4o failure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance reporting: Pass@1 for RIMO-N and average fraction-completed for RIMO-P
rubrics_metrics.description: RIMO-N results are reported as Pass@1 accuracy (%). RIMO-P final performance score P is computed as P = (1/N) Σ_i (Si/Xi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report deterministic Pass@1 for integer-track items. For proof track, report average proportion of consecutively-completed sub-steps (P) to reflect stepwise reasoning capability rather than binary final correctness alone.
